<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 041a120b6189e9b174a3f4b8cf6202f22ace2bbd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

```sh

git fetch origin 74bc6aa80f1c163ab83ef1fedc75dc67e730d643 && git checkout 74bc6aa80f1c163ab83ef1fedc75dc67e730d643
```

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than

> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 041a120b6189e9b174a3f4b8cf6202f22ace2bbd` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5a9bf414cf27e307083bde55bd0f66884398d2a8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.flow-run-as-system-identity-assignment-write-refused.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/flow-system-identity-write-refusal.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/errors.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/runtime-identity.ts (all on `origin/main` as #25483 left them), packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/README.md, packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template, .changeset/25554-runas-identity-assignment-wording.md, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs

Record rendered at 2026-10-24T01:00Z against card #25554 (body and both comments), PR #25564 (body, five files, net diff against `origin/main`), ruling 6354966423 and the six other comments on #25251, and the check-runs on the head. The remainder of the diff (`content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx`, `content/docs/references/automation/flow.mdx`: regenerated projections of the describe) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

**J1 — the describe sentence states what #25483 enforces, no more and no less: RIGHT.** Compared clause by clause against the merged code on `main`:
- Predicate. `assertFlowSystemIdentityWriteAllowed` returns unless `context.isSystem` AND `context.flowRunId` are both truthy; `resolveRunDataContext` hands a `runAs: 'system'` run's data nodes `{ isSystem: true, actor, flowRunId, … }`. The describe scopes the refusal to "a system run's governed writes"; the source comment above the key spells the predicate (`isSystem` AND a `flowRunId`, ahead of the `isSystem` bypass). Matches.
- Objects. `FLOW_SYSTEM_IDENTITY_WRITE_OBJECTS` = `sys_user_position`, `sys_user_permission_set`, `sys_invitation`, `sys_member`. The describe names the same four. Matches.
- Verbs. The refusal reads `GOVERNED_OPERATIONS` exported from `delegated-admin-gate.ts` = `insert`, `update`, `delete`, `transfer`, `restore`, `purge`. The describe lists the same six. Matches. (A verb added to the gate is refused by #25483 and would need a describe edit; that coupling is noted in the gate's own docblock.)
- Error. `PermissionDeniedError`, `code = 'PERMISSION_DENIED'`, `status 403`. The describe says `PERMISSION_DENIED`; the comment and the D3 entry add the 403. Matches.
- Remedies. `ASSIGNMENT_PRESCRIPTION` (the two assignment tables → `runAs: 'user'`, the D12 gate judges the acting user and stamps `granted_by`) and `MEMBERSHIP_PRESCRIPTION` (invitations and memberships → the organization endpoints). The describe says exactly that split, with the ADR-0090 D12 citation. Matches.
- Unchanged set. Reads of the four, writes to every other object, a `runAs: 'user'` run, and a platform writer whose `isSystem` context carries no `flowRunId`. The describe's new sentence says nothing about non-run writers, so it claims nothing false; the source comment states "a platform writer whose system context carries no flow run is unchanged" and the D3 entry's `reason` enumerates them (seeders, better-auth and its reconciliation, invitation placement, the organization-administrator grant). Right: a flow author is never a flow-less platform writer, so the describe does not owe that clause; the card's item 1 wording is met across the describe plus its comment block.
- Position. The sentence sits after "system flows keep system privileges; after an approval decision…" and before the no-trigger-user clause. The retained "keep system privileges" phrase is now qualified in the same string, so the published contract no longer states the rule without its exception. Right.
- No key, default, enum value or accept-set moves: the `flow.zod.ts` hunk is a comment block and a longer `.describe()` string only. `Clause-②: no` is the right line.

**J2 — the ADR-0087 D3 semantic entry: RIGHT.** Shape per `entries/README.md`: one file, named `18.` plus the entry id plus `.ts`, the filename derived from `id` (`flow-run-as-system-identity-assignment-write-refused`), copyright header, type-only import, `export const entry: SemanticMigration` with `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`; no `conversionIds` (no D2 conversion exists, and none should: flipping `runAs` changes every other node's authority and an endpoint call is a new call, not a rewrite), no `relevantWhen` (so it is always listed, correct for a surface the stack question cannot prove absent). `surface` carries no backtick and no pipe, as the upgrade-guide renderer requires; it is prose like the step-18 siblings (`visibility-predicate-has-argument-refused`), not the dotted form the type's example gives, which the registry accepts. Step number 18 is right: `@objectstack/spec` is `18.0.0` and `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is `18.0.0` on the head, so the change of meaning lands inside protocol 18 and belongs to `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR[18].semantic`. No `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment was added to `registry.ts.template`; none is owed (290 of the 417 step-18 semantic entries on the head carry none). `registry.ts`, `spec-changes.json` and the upgrade guide are generated and git-ignored, so nothing further is owed in the tree. The entry's `reason` repeats #25483's behaviour (predicate, six verbs, four objects, 403, any depth including cascade legs and hook writes, the unchanged set, the zero census) and matches the merged module's docblock.

**J3 — regenerated projections: RIGHT.** The two `.mdx` tables carry the new describe text verbatim in every `runAs` row they render (five rows in `automation-api.mdx`, two in `flow.mdx`). A scan of `skills/**` and `content/docs/**` on the head finds no other copy of the describe string, consistent with the dev's "no diff" from `gen:skill-refs` and `gen:skill-docs`.

**J4 — the changeset marker.** The changeset is not declared breaking (no BREAKING banner, no `!`, `minor`), so `check-adr-0087-registration` does not judge it (its G1 case). It carries the `adr-0087: registered` marker anyway, naming the entry id; harmless and truthful, and `Lint & Repo Gates` concluded success on the head.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` `minor`, with `Clause-②: no (describe text and ADR registration only; no accept-set change)` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic (records the change of meaning #25483 landed)` on the PR body and the changeset, verbatim as the claim. RIGHT. The dispatch order said `patch`; the gate wins, and the gate is as the dev cites it: `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` header, "THE LEVEL AXIS (#16055; re-ruled by maintainer ruling A, 2026-10-21, on #25105) — the level follows the METADATA PROTOCOL alone … a declared kind must grade AT LEAST ONE package whose published source it moves `minor` or above; a declared `none` must grade every entry it introduces `patch`". A `semantic` declaration at `patch` would have been refused; `Check Changeset` concluded success on the head. The ADR-0087 same-release condition is a release matter, not a level one: #25483 (`@objectstack/plugin-security` `minor` with `!`) is on `main`, this PR's D3 entry must ship in the same release, and the maintainer has paused the release cut (project timeline) until it does.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. `minor` not `patch` — answered above, RIGHT.
2. ADR-0073 amendment left out as Tier H — RIGHT to leave out: `docs/adr/**` is on the governed list (`check-governed-merges.mjs`, ruled 2026-09-18; CODEOWNERS `/docs/adr/`), so it lands by a maintainer merge and must not hold items 1 and 2. The draft at `/mnt/project-files/spec-seat-1/out/25554-adr-0073-amendment-draft.md` was read. Its substance is right: it targets the one bullet that is now false (line 155 on `main`, "`runAs:'system'` stays god-mode throughout"), states the predicate, the six verbs, the four objects, the 403 ahead of the bypass, both remedies with the D12 citation, and the flow-less system writer as unchanged, and it dates and cites the ruling and both PRs. Two wording points for whoever routes it: (a) the ADR's existing amendment convention (the #3760 amendment) is a dated `## Amendment:` section near the top plus a strike-through at the falsified sentence; the draft is an in-place bold parenthetical only, so the router should either add the short dated section or accept the lighter form knowingly; (b) line 24 of the ADR ("elevating would have widened these runs (e.g. letting them write `sys_user_position`)") is still true for an `isSystem` context without a `flowRunId` but now reads as if a system flow could write that table; one trailing clause there would close it. Neither point touches this PR.
3. The describe sentence omits the platform-writer clause — answered in J1, RIGHT.

Escalations, none of which blocks this head:
- E1 (maintainer, governed): the "Landed PR1" record 6371045455 on #25251 names TWO ADR edits as open with the maintainer — ADR-0073 M2 and the ADR-0096 D5 row ("the empty-principal skip … keeps exactly one behavior: honoring `SystemGrant`/`isSystem`", now true with one carve-out). Card #25554 carries only ADR-0073. Both are `docs/adr/**`, Tier H, outside this PR's surface; the seat routing the ADR-0073 draft should carry the ADR-0096 D5 sentence in the same maintainer PR or ask the maintainer whether it is owed.
- E2 (lane seat / devx): `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` line 76 (the hand-written `runAs` row) and the access-recipes and approvals pages still describe `runAs: 'system'` as "elevated, bypasses RLS" with no mention of the identity-object refusal. PR1's dev-report flagged it with "carrier: PR2 (its describe sentence) or a devx docs pass". It is not in card #25554's declared surface (generated reference pages and `skills/**`), it is true for ordinary records, and the generated reference now states the exception; so it is a follow-up docs pass, not a defect of this head.
- E3 (release): the maintainer's timeline entry stands — no 18.1.0 cut until this PR is on `main` beside #25483.
